_meta.product_category: Supermarket grocery retail, weekly household shop
_meta.purpose: FRESH-DATA VALIDITY TEST (n=50 across 11 categories). The competitive set is derived per PRODUCT CATEGORY and held constant across its members, so the business is the only variable.
_meta.LABEL_SOURCE: Published: 48 stores; DFI once held a near-monopoly in premium but FairPrice Finest expanded 9->39 stores; now owned by Macrovalue
sources: Published: 48 stores; DFI once held a near-monopoly in premium but FairPrice Finest expanded 9->39 stores; now owned by Macrovalue
_meta.authoring_note: FORM DATA reconstructed by the analyst from public sources. The LABEL is external and published; the form is thinner than a real submission. This is the known weakness of the test.

form.category: Supermarket grocery retail, weekly household shop
form.differentiator: The premium grocery shop. Imported and specialty lines you will not find at the value chains.
form.undercut_on: We no longer own premium. FairPrice Finest has 39 stores against our 48 and is closing the gap.
form.their_price_point: See the derived competitive set for the category price ladder.

tier_0_default.why: Cheaper or no purchase at all.

tier_1_cheap_substitute.why: Lowest shelf price for the same basket.

tier_2_direct_set.why: Same product: a weekly grocery basket. 691 stores islandwide.

members: NTUC FairPrice - the national default, 125 stores
tier_3_category_incumbent.why: FairPrice owns 'default', Sheng Siong owns 'value+fresh', Cold Storage owns 'premium'.

tier_4_adjacent_crossover.why: Same need (feed the household) via a different channel.

tier_7_new_entrants.why: Derived from new openings and the DFI ownership change.

derived_competitive_set._derivation_method: Derived from the PRODUCT CATEGORY (Supermarket grocery retail, weekly household shop), not the owner's list. Price spread in this category: moderate (premium vs value shelf). Tiers follow the eight-tier frame: default/no-purchase, cheap substitute, direct set, category incumbent (the rungs of the customer's mental ladder), adjacent crossover, indirect, and new entrants derived from public opening records.
